finding: Does joint inference improve recovery across a goal hierarchy? Joint reading improves internal-node probability forecasts over the one-direction ablations, but bottom-up inference already matches it at the root. Removing distant evidence can hurt more than removing immediate-child evidence, and root accuracy is not monotone in every coverage series. These are finite constructed-tree results: marginal node scores do not establish a joint-prediction advantage or mathematical smoothness.
